title: The Tryouts of Lake Minnow
premise: Jude Underhill, a scholarship student at Lake Minnow Academy, has spent her life being careful — careful with money, with feelings, with the truth about her dead parents. When she inherits her grandmother's recipe box and finds a card that isn't a recipe but a summons to the Tryouts, a century-old tradition that secretly chooses the town's 'Keepers,' Jude discovers the academy's scholarships are funded by a bargain the town made long ago. The Tryouts are rigged this year: the founding families plan to end them, dissolve the Keepers, and sell the lake rights that keep Lake Minnow alive. With the help of Theo Vance — heir to one of those families, and the boy she absolutely should not be falling for — Jude must enter the Tryouts herself, expose the rigging before the last game of the season, and choose between the inheritance of duty and the family she builds along the way. In the end, the Tryouts are saved by being rewritten: Jude becomes the first Keeper chosen from outside the founding bloodlines, and the town — not the families — holds the lake.
about_author: Mirabel Okonkwo grew up in a small lakeside town where every summer festival felt like it was hiding something, which is probably why she writes about secrets. She now lives two towns over from a real Lake Minnow and still checks recipe boxes for messages.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. On the anniversary of her grandmother's funeral, Jude sorts through the recipe box she inherited and finds a cream-colored card with no ingredients — only instructions, a date, and the word TRYOUTS. When she touches it, the kitchen lights flicker and the card grows warm. Emotional beat: grief cracking open into wonder; the careful life begins to loosen.

chapters.title: Scholarship Terms
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At Lake Minnow Academy, Jude reviews her scholarship paperwork for the hundredth time and notices a clause she never read: continued funding 'contingent upon participation in seasonal obligations.' Her friend Priya jokes that the school owns her soul. Jude laughs, but the word 'obligations' itches like the card in her backpack. Beat: dread disguised as normalcy.

chapters.title: The Boy at the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo Vance watches Jude photograph the boathouse where his family's name is carved into every beam. He knows what the card in her bag means — he's seen one before, the year his older brother vanished from town. He decides not to warn her. Beat: guilt introduced; the love interest arrives already compromised.

chapters.title: Card Number Two
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A second card appears inside Jude's locker, addressed in her grandmother's handwriting though Gran has been dead a year. It lists a time, a place — the old grange hall — and a warning: DON'T TELL THE FAMILIES. Jude goes, alone, against every careful instinct she owns. Beat: fear outranked by longing for connection.

chapters.title: The Grange Hall
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In the dust-choked grange hall, Jude meets three other card-holders: Priya (a card-holder after all), a groundskeeper's son named Marcus, and an elderly woman, Mrs. Okafor, who claims to be a former Keeper. They explain the Tryouts: a hidden competition that selects the town's protectors. Beat: found family's first assembly; awe shadowed by unease.

chapters.title: What the Families Buried
chapters.summary: Mrs. Okafor's POV. A flashback chapter: 1974, when the founding families signed the Accord trading lake rights for the academy's fortune, with the Keepers as enforcement. Mrs. Okafor was the last Keeper chosen from outside the bloodlines — and the last one they ever allowed. Beat: history as warning; the scale of the secret revealed.

chapters.title: Theo Lying Beautifully
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Theo asks Jude to study with him, charming and attentive, while clearly fishing for what she knows. She lies back, testing him, and hates how good they are together. That night she finds her grandmother's name on a Keeper roster in the academy archive — and Theo's mother's signature beneath the Accord. Beat: attraction entangled with betrayal.

chapters.title: First Trial
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The four candidates face their first trial at midnight on the frozen inlet: retrieve a token from under the ice without breaking it. Marcus nearly drowns; Jude saves him using an instinct she can't explain — Gran's muscle memory living in her hands. Beat: competence discovered; the team bonds through shared danger.

chapters.title: The Rigging
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya, who works in the admissions office, finds altered Tryout records: this year's trials have been pre-scored so no outsider can win. The founding families intend to fail all four candidates, declare the tradition broken, and dissolve the Keepers forever. Beat: stakes sharpened from personal to civic; quiet fury.

chapters.title: Dinner with the Vances
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Theo invites Jude to dinner at Vance House, where his mother, Eleanor, interrogates her with velvet courtesy and offers her a full-ride 'legacy scholarship' — if she withdraws from whatever she's been invited into. Jude refuses. On the porch afterward, Theo kisses her and immediately looks destroyed by it. Beat: love against duty made literal.

chapters.title: Gran's Third Card
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Following clues in Gran's recipes — measurements that are coordinates, oven temperatures that are dates — Jude finds a third card hidden in the church organ bench. It reveals Gran wasn't just a Keeper; she was the one who hid the Accord's original document, the thing that proves the families' claim is fraudulent. Beat: inheritance redefined as mission.

chapters.title: The Vanishing
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confronts his brother Daniel — alive, hiding in the next county, exiled for refusing to help rig the Tryouts years ago. Daniel tells him Eleanor will ruin Jude the way she ruined him. Theo must choose: family loyalty or the girl. Beat: the love interest crosses the line; he picks her, secretly.

chapters.title: Second Trial
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The second trial tests honesty: each candidate must confess their worst act before the old grange mirror, which shows truth. Priya admits she reported a teacher to save her own scholarship; Marcus admits he's been feeding information to Eleanor. The group fractures. Beat: trust broken from within; lowest point approaching.

chapters.title: Expulsion Papers
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Eleanor moves early: Jude is summoned and shown expulsion papers citing 'unauthorized archive access.' The scholarship, the school, the future she built carefully for twenty years — gone unless she signs a withdrawal. Jude asks for one night to decide. Beat: everything she was careful for threatened at once.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Last Game
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo gives Jude the Accord's location — his mother's study safe — and burns his own legacy letter in her sink. They spend the night planning instead of sleeping, hands almost touching, everything unsaid finally said without words. Beat: love fully declared through action; calm before the climax.

chapters.title: Theft at Vance House
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. During the homecoming gala, Jude and Priya infiltrate Vance House. Jude opens the safe using the combination hidden in Gran's pie crust recipe — Gran planned this rescue decades ago. They get the Accord out seconds before Eleanor walks in. Beat: triumph laced with terror; the trap half-sprung.

chapters.title: Caught
chapters.summary: Eleanor's POV. Eleanor catches Marcus, flips him fully, and learns everything: the theft, the plan, Theo's betrayal. At halftime of the last game, she takes the microphone to announce the Tryouts' dissolution and Jude's expulsion — turning the whole town into her courtroom. Beat: villain seizes the stage; despair peaks.

chapters.title: Halftime
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In front of the entire town, Jude reads the Accord aloud: the lake belongs to whoever keeps it, not to any bloodline — and the Keepers were never the families' to dissolve. Mrs. Okafor stands beside her; then Marcus, confessing; then dozens of townspeople who owe the Keepers quietly across generations. Beat: public reckoning; courage contagious.

chapters.title: The Last Trial
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, braided. Eleanor demands the tradition be settled properly: one final trial, tonight, on the lake. Jude faces it alone against the families' champion — Theo, forced onto the ice. Instead of competing, he forfeits, naming Jude worthy. The old magic of the Tryouts accepts the gesture. Beat: climax resolved by sacrifice, not victory.

chapters.title: Keeper
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. By dawn, the town council ratifies a new Accord: the Tryouts continue, opened to everyone, with Jude as the youngest Head Keeper in a century. Eleanor concedes with icy grace; Daniel comes home. Jude places Gran's recipe cards in the grange hall archive — the first entries in a public record. Beat: inheritance fulfilled and transformed.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Weeks later, Theo and Jude repaint the boathouse, adding new names beside the old carved ones — Priya, Marcus, Mrs. Okafor, and space left blank for whoever comes next. Their romance is tentative, honest, unrigged. Beat: tenderness earned; the found family settles into its shape.

chapters.title: A New Card
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Spring. Jude opens the recipe box to add her own first card and finds a fresh one waiting in Gran's handwriting: a single line — 'Told you you'd stop being careful.' Jude laughs until she cries, then writes her own instructions for whoever inherits the box next. Beat: grief transmuted into legacy; the story closes on an open hand.
